questions.questionText:
Statement:
A massive landslide on the national highway has severed connectivity to several mountainous villages and stranded hundreds of tourists.

Courses of Action:
I. The disaster management authority should immediately dispatch earthmoving equipment and rescue teams to clear the highway and provide food and medical aid to stranded travelers.
II. All permanent residents of the mountainous villages should be permanently relocated to other states.
options: Only course of action I follows
Both course of action I and II follow
Neither course of action I nor II follows
Only course of action II follows
questions.hint: A course of action must be feasible, address the root problem, and avoid extreme overreactions.
questions.explanation: Course of Action I is an immediate, practical, and constructive disaster response. Course of Action II is a wildly disproportionate and impractical extreme overreaction.
solutionSteps: Step 1: Identify the exact problem stated in the premise.
Step 2: Evaluate Action I: Is it practical, positive, and does it alleviate the problem?
Step 3: Evaluate Action II: Does it introduce an extreme overreaction or create worse problems?
Step 4: Select Only course of action I follows.
questions.memoryTip: Course of Action Rules: 1. Practicality, 2. Proportionality (no extreme measures), 3. Effective reduction of the problem.

questions.questionText:
Statement:
Reports indicate a spike in cyber fraud cases where senior citizens are duped of their retirement savings through fake investment apps.

II. All internet banking and digital financial transactions should be banned for individuals above 60 years of age.

Statement:

Reports indicate a spike in cyber fraud cases where senior citizens are duped of their retirement savings through fake investment apps.

Courses of Action:
I. The cyber police and banking regulator should conduct targeted financial awareness drives and launch a dedicated rapid-response helpline for cyber fraud.
II. All internet banking and digital financial transactions should be banned for individuals above 60 years of age.
options: Neither course of action I nor II follows
Only course of action II follows
Both course of action I and II follow
Only course of action I follows
questions.hint: Punishing the victims by restricting basic rights is never a valid administrative course of action.
questions.explanation: Action I provides constructive education and rapid redressal. Action II discriminates against senior citizens and paralyzes normal banking access instead of solving cybercrime.
solutionSteps: Step 1: Identify the exact problem stated in the premise.
Step 2: Evaluate Action I: Is it practical, positive, and does it alleviate the problem?
Step 3: Evaluate Action II: Does it introduce an extreme overreaction or create worse problems?
Step 4: Select Only course of action I follows.
questions.memoryTip: Course of Action Rules: 1. Practicality, 2. Proportionality (no extreme measures), 3. Effective reduction of the problem.

questions.questionText:
Statement:
Waterlogging during every monsoon season leads to acute traffic snarls and spread of vector-borne illnesses in the old city quarter.

Courses of Action:
I. The municipal corporation should desilt and widen underground storm-water drains well before the onset of monsoon.

Waterlogging during every monsoon season leads to acute traffic snarls and spread of vector-borne illnesses in the old city quarter.

Courses of Action:
I. The municipal corporation should desilt and widen underground storm-water drains well before the onset of monsoon.
II. Civic teams should conduct regular health inspections and penalize properties allowing stagnant open water pooling.
options: Neither course of action I nor II follows
Only course of action II follows
Only course of action I follows
Both course of action I and II follow
questions.hint: Preventative infrastructure maintenance combined with public compliance enforcement are standard dual courses of action.
questions.explanation: Action I addresses the root infrastructural bottleneck (clogged drains), and Action II enforces preventative public health hygiene. Both actions are constructive, feasible, and follow.
solutionSteps: Step 1: Identify the exact problem stated in the premise.
Step 2: Evaluate Action I: Is it practical, positive, and does it alleviate the problem?
Step 3: Evaluate Action II: Does it introduce an extreme overreaction or create worse problems?
Step 4: Select Both course of action I and II follow.
questions.memoryTip: Course of Action Rules: 1. Practicality, 2. Proportionality (no extreme measures), 3. Effective reduction of the problem.

questions.questionText:
Statement:
A premier government research hospital is experiencing acute shortages of life-saving cancer medications due to global supply chain disruptions.

Courses of Action:
I. Hospital management should explore emergency procurement from alternative certified domestic pharmaceutical manufacturers.
II. The hospital should turn away all existing oncology patients until international supplies normalize.
options: Both course of action I and II follow
Only course of action I follows
Neither course of action I nor II follows
Only course of action II follows
questions.hint: Courses of action must prioritize human life and continuity of essential public services.
questions.explanation: Action I seeks alternative procurement to save lives (Constructive). Action II violates medical ethics and neglects patient duty (Unacceptable).

Step 2: Evaluate Action I: Is it practical, positive, and does it alleviate the problem?
Step 3: Evaluate Action II: Does it introduce an extreme overreaction or create worse problems?

questions.questionText:
Statement:
A massive landslide on the national highway has severed connectivity to several mountainous villages and stranded hundreds of tourists.

Courses of Action:
I. The disaster management authority should immediately dispatch earthmoving equipment and rescue teams to clear the highway and provide food and medical aid to stranded travelers.
II. All permanent residents of the mountainous villages should be permanently relocated to other states.
options: Only course of action I follows
Neither course of action I nor II follows
Both course of action I and II follow
Only course of action II follows
questions.hint: A course of action must be feasible, address the root problem, and avoid extreme overreactions.
questions.explanation: Course of Action I is an immediate, practical, and constructive disaster response. Course of Action II is a wildly disproportionate and impractical extreme overreaction.
solutionSteps: Step 1: Identify the exact problem stated in the premise.
Step 2: Evaluate Action I: Is it practical, positive, and does it alleviate the problem?
Step 3: Evaluate Action II: Does it introduce an extreme overreaction or create worse problems?
Step 4: Select Only course of action I follows.
questions.memoryTip: Course of Action Rules: 1. Practicality, 2. Proportionality (no extreme measures), 3. Effective reduction of the problem.

questions.questionText:
Statement:
Reports indicate a spike in cyber fraud cases where senior citizens are duped of their retirement savings through fake investment apps.

Courses of Action:
I. The cyber police and banking regulator should conduct targeted financial awareness drives and launch a dedicated rapid-response helpline for cyber fraud.
II. All internet banking and digital financial transactions should be banned for individuals above 60 years of age.
options: Both course of action I and II follow
Only course of action I follows
Neither course of action I nor II follows
Only course of action II follows
questions.hint: Punishing the victims by restricting basic rights is never a valid administrative course of action.
questions.explanation: Action I provides constructive education and rapid redressal. Action II discriminates against senior citizens and paralyzes normal banking access instead of solving cybercrime.
